question: People tracking white shapes miss an unexpected cross. What property of the cross decides whether they see it?
answer: How closely it resembles what they are tracking. Most and colleagues had people follow white shapes and ignore black ones. An unexpected white cross was usually noticed; a black one, matching the ignored set, was mostly missed, and grey fell between. Attention filters by feature, and the filter hides whatever matches the rejected pile.
move: What gets missed is whatever looks like the things being ignored.
ask: What do I overlook because it looks like all the things I have learned to ignore?
reference: Most, Simons, Scholl, Jimenez, Clifford & Chabris, How not to be seen: the contribution of similarity and selective ignoring to sustained inattentional blindness, Psychological Science, 2001
